condition.label: Piriformis syndrome
condition.distinctions: Selected piriformis-related sciatic irritation label, not all deep gluteal syndrome, discogenic radicular pain, proximal hamstring pathology or nonspecific buttock pain. Clinical attribution remains uncertain; no self-diagnostic test is supplied.

scope.population: Adults with clinically assessed piriformis syndrome; study-specific populations retained per source.
scope.stage: Conservative care candidates; severity and symptom duration insufficiently characterized.
scope.operativeStatus: No postoperative protocol extracted; do not infer operative clearance.
scope.exclusions: Do not apply to unassessed sciatica-like symptoms or other diagnoses by label alone. Trial exclusions are applicability limits, not universal contraindications.
scope.uncertainty: A condition label does not select an individual stretch, dose or range. No clinical reviewer is identified.

sources.design: Assessor-blind randomized three-group trial; 45 participants, 15/group; retrospectively registered.
sources.population: Adults 18–60 with low-back pain, positive FAIR and piriformis tenderness. Other lumbar/hip pathologies and recent hip/knee injuries excluded; operative status not reported.
sources.comparator: Foam-roller compression or no added exercise.
sources.coInterventions: All groups: heat 15 min and TENS 15 min.
sources.outcomes: No between-group pain or calf sEMG benefit. Disability favored stretching versus compression: MD −12.62, 95% CI −20.41 to −4.38, p=0.009.
sources.followUp: Pre/post ten treatment sessions; later follow-up not reported.
sources.uncertainty: Small groups; participants unblinded; sex imbalance; broad DGS label. Narrative conclusion broader than its explicit pairwise result; do not assert superiority versus control.
sources.harms: not reported; no loss to follow-up is not a harms assessment.
sources.limitations: Indirect for piriformis-only diagnosis; multimodal supervised care does not establish a self-directed app routine or universal contraindications.

protocol.execution: Supine, unaffected foot on wall; affected ankle above opposite kneecap; arms alongside, palms down; slight stretch.
protocol.dose: 3 sets × 2 minutes; 2 minutes rest between sets.

sources.design: Prospective observational, nonrandomized; 44 adults, 22/group; allocation by accepting dry needling.
sources.population: Adults 18–70 with clinically assessed unilateral piriformis muscle syndrome after alternative hip/lumbar/sacroiliac causes excluded; pain persisted after oral treatment. Stage and operative status not reported.
sources.coInterventions: Exercise arm: stretching, bilateral bridging, flexed hip/knee feet-together leg raises, posture/activity advice; medication use during follow-up not reported.
sources.outcomes: Within-group improvement in VAS, ODI, LEFS and DN4; no significant between-group follow-up differences. No untreated comparator or isolated component test.
sources.uncertainty: Confounding, sex imbalance, no untreated control. Baseline ODI direction conflicts between narrative and Table 2; do not resolve by guessing.
sources.harms: No adverse effects stated for needling arm; exercise-specific harms not reported.
sources.limitations: Bundled program cannot establish independent benefit of a stretch or bridge; exclusion criteria are not universal exercise prohibitions.

protocol.execution: Static self-stretch position unspecified; bilateral bridging; side leg raises with hip/knee flexion 45 degrees, feet together.
protocol.dose: Stretch hold 30 seconds; wording: 10 repetitions/sets. Bridge/leg-raise dose not reported.
protocol.frequency: Stretch twice daily; exercise program 3 weeks.
protocol.supervision: Home program taught by therapist with image handout; ongoing supervision not reported.
